description: Describe a playback order in plain language and have one written and validated. Pass the playlist it is for as playlistId: the order is written against that playlist's REAL items, so leaving it out produces a rule aimed at nothing. Creating does NOT apply it — assign_playlist_order does. Read `status` on the result: READY = usable; INVALID = written but it failed validation, and `diagnostics` say why (refine it, this is not a transport error); MESSAGE = a clarifying question or refusal, nothing was produced; PENDING = still running, poll get_playlist_order. The answer, under createOrderSequencer, also has sequencer (the order: id oseq_..., name, latestReadyVersionID) and version (the version written, or null).

description.description: A note about the order shown to the user beside its name; it does not change how the order plays.

intent.description: What the order should do, in plain language — e.g. 'always start with the welcome clip, then alternate a talk and a song, and never play the same song twice in a row'.

name.description: Short name for the order, e.g. 'Sunday service running order'.

playlistId.description: The playlist (pl_...) this order is for. Omitting it produces a rule with no items to reason about.

name: create_playlist_order

diagnostics.description: Each problem: stage, code, message, line.

status.description: READY: usable; INVALID: failed validation; MESSAGE: a question or refusal, nothing produced; PENDING: still running.

version.description: The version written, or null when nothing was produced.

code.description: Stable — branch on it: INVALID_INPUT, REVISION_REQUIRED, STALE_PUBLISH, CONFIRM_REQUIRED, UNAVAILABLE, …

currentRevision.description: CONFLICT: the revision it has now

detail.description: What is wrong, in a sentence

errors.description: Each problem, when a check refused it

title: Create playlist order
